method: Second-pass checks against freshly retrieved publisher release notes, model documentation and launch posts. Exact identity and external availability were checked separately from document publication dates. This is a four-record sample, not a complete re-audit.

items.identity_and_availability: The May 10, 2023 Vertex AI release note explicitly lists text-bison@001 and chat-bison@001 in the newly available preview, with API, console and SDK access. This supports the exact text-bison checkpoint and date rather than only the PaLM 2 family announcement.

The October 6, 2025 API changelog announces gpt-audio-mini as a newly released speech-to-speech model. The January 13, 2026 changelog identifies the previous alias target as gpt-audio-mini-2025-10-06, and the model page independently lists that snapshot. Text and audio input/output are documented. The snapshot date is therefore corroborated by a dated launch entry, not inferred solely from its name.
items.limitation: Current model documentation describes the family after later updates; it is not proof that every present capability or limit existed in the initial snapshot. The catalog already notes that this snapshot later shut down.

items.identity_and_availability: Google's August 26 launch post makes the preview available immediately through Gemini API, AI Studio and Vertex AI, names gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview in its example, and handles both text and image response parts. The API changelog confirms the preview date. The October 2 launch post and changelog document general availability. Current model documentation lists stable and deprecated-preview names within the same model family and explicitly supports text plus image outputs.
items.limitation: The record consolidates preview and stable names without claiming that their underlying weights are proven identical. A separate trained revision would require additional publisher evidence. Current context limits need not match the initial preview; the catalog already says so.

items.identity_and_availability: The July 29 API release note explicitly says grok-voice-2.0 is available. The dated publisher launch post describes training changes and speech-to-speech conversation, supporting a new trained model rather than a serving tier. August 5 is the later mutable-alias migration, not the first availability date. The API documentation supports audio and text responses and distinguishes the dedicated speech-to-text service.
